In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
molecular dynamics simulation is a powerful tool for the investigation of the effect of mutation on the conformation and stability of the cytoplamic domain of PLB.
the simulations show that the cytoplasm domain of PLB has an intrinsic helical propensity, which can be disrupted upon phosphorylation and/or mutation.
the molecular dynamics simulations are in agreement with available experimental data and that the simulations are useful in elucidating the structural basis of the effect of mutations on PLB.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phosphorylation of PLB and mutation of R9C result in partial unfolding of the helical domain, which in turn results in loss of inhibitory activity.
phosphorylation or mutation of PLB causes the cytoplasm helix to unfold, and this is the mechanism by which PLB loses its ability to regulate the calcium pump.
phosphorylation of PLB at Ser-16 and the R9C mutant of PLB are not able to maintain the same level of helical propensity as the unphosphorylate wild-type peptide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytoplasm helix of PLN is a highly dynamic structure, and the helical propensity is highly sensitive to the surrounding sequence environment.
molecular dynamics simulations can be used to investigate the effects of phosphorylation and other post-translational modifications on the structure and function of small proteins.
the cytoplasm helix of PLN is not a stable alpha-helix.
